post.summary: Creates an uptime check.
post.description:
The check starts running as soon as it is created: it is scheduled in the monitoring region
named by `RegionId`, the same way the app schedules one.
            
`Target` has to match `TypeId` - ICMP takes `Ip`, TCP takes `Ip` and
`Port`, HTTP takes `Url` - and sending a field belonging to another type is
rejected rather than ignored.

get.summary: Gets a single uptime check by id.

parameters.name: checkId
parameters.description: Uptime check identifier.

patch.summary: Updates an uptime check. Send only the fields you want to change.
patch.description:
An omitted field is left alone, and re-sending a value the check already holds is a no-op
rather than an error. Sending nothing at all is a 400.
            
`TagIds` replaces the check's tags outright; an empty array clears them. Changing
`TypeId` requires a `Target` for the new type, because the two are stored
together and the old target would not fit.
            
`MaintenanceMode` starts or ends a maintenance window for this check. Omit it to
leave the current state alone; send `Enabled: true` with a start, a duration and a
reason to begin one, or `Enabled: false` on its own to end it. A duration of zero
means the window does not expire on its own.

parameters.name: checkId
parameters.description: Uptime check to update.

delete.description:
This is the same delete the app performs: the check is deactivated rather than removed, its
monitoring schedule is cancelled in the region that runs it, and its cached status is cleared.
Deleting an already-deleted check succeeds, so a retried request is safe.

parameters.name: checkId
parameters.description: Uptime check to delete.

post.summary: Uploads a file and returns a link to it.
post.description:
Send it as `multipart/form-data` with the file part named `file`, plus
`itemType` (`Ticket`, `Task` or `Project`) and `itemId`.
            
The record has to exist and be yours - an upload against an unknown id is a 404 rather
than an orphaned file nothing will ever reference.
            
The returned url carries a time-limited access token. Pass the **name and url together**
to a comment endpoint to attach the file; the token is stripped before storage and a
fresh one issued on every read, so do not store the url yourself.
            
The largest accepted upload is 44 MB.

get.summary: Downloads the rendered PDF for an invoice.
get.description:
The only endpoint whose success response is not a `BaseResponse<T>` envelope: a
200 is the PDF itself, `application/pdf`, as a file download named after the invoice's
display number (e.g. `INV-1042.pdf`). Errors still use the envelope.


The document is rendered on demand from the invoice's current data and template, so it
reflects the invoice at request time rather than a stored copy. Each successful download is
recorded against the invoice as an export event.

parameters.name: invoiceId
parameters.description: Invoice identifier.

get.summary:
Lists the billing roles configured for the service provider. Use a role's Id as
BillingRoleId when logging time against a ticket.

Lists the work types configured for the service provider. Use a work type's Id as
WorkTypeId when logging time against a ticket.
Lists the tax rates configured for the service provider.
get.description:
Read-only. Tax rates usually originate in the connected accounting system (Xero or
QuickBooks) rather than being managed in Gorelo, so there is no create, update or delete
here.


This is the lookup for every tax reference the API emits: a product category's
`TaxId` and a contract line item's `Tax.Id` are the same identifier as
`Id` here, so a tax seen on any endpoint is resolved by finding it in this list.

`Percentage` is the rate itself and `IsDefault` marks the rate applied when none
is chosen. Only active rates are listed; a service provider with none configured gets an
empty list rather than a 404.

`SubTaxes` carries the component rates a tax is broken into, for accounting systems
that split one tax into parts - HST as GST plus PST, for example - and is an empty array
for the common case of a tax with no components. Where components exist they are what
gets charged: the amount is the sum of each component's `Percentage`, and the
parent's own `Percentage` is not applied on top of them. Only active components are
listed.

get.summary: Lists logged time across every ticket and task, narrowed by any of the filters.
get.description:
One flat collection rather than a list per ticket, because time is pulled across tickets for
billing sync, reporting and dashboards. Pass `ticketIds` to get a single ticket's time.


Every filter is optional and combining two narrows to the entries that satisfy both. Each id
filter is a comma-separated list and an entry matches if its id is any of them; a value that
is not an id is rejected with 400. A well-formed value that matches nothing — a client id
that does not exist, a ticket with no logged time — is an empty page, not a 404. Timestamps
are UTC; each `...Since` bound includes the instant it names and each `...Before`
bound excludes it, so two windows sharing an edge tile instead of both returning the entry
on it.

`ActualHours` is the duration actually logged. `AdjustedHours` is the duration after
the work type's minimum and increment rounding, and is null when no rounding applied — in
that case the billed duration is simply `ActualHours`.


Each entry names what it was logged against: an entry hangs off either a ticket or a task, so
one of `Ticket` and `Task` carries the id, number and title, and the other is null.

parameters.name: Cursor
parameters.description: Opaque pagination cursor from a previous page; omit for the first page. Only valid against the same filters that produced it.

parameters.description: Number of items per page. Clamped to 1–200 (default 50).

post.summary: Logs time against a ticket.
post.description:
StartedOn and EndedOn are single UTC instants and ActualHours is decimal hours. Supply any two
of the three and the third is derived; sending all three is accepted only when ActualHours
agrees with the span between the two instants.


The logged duration is rounded up by the work type's minimum and increment, so the billed
duration can exceed the elapsed time between start and end. Supplying a ServiceLineId
prices the entry against that contract and moves its hour allowance: a BlockHours contract
has the entry's hours drawn down, and a LimitedHours contract covers the entry up to its
remaining allowance and bills only the overage beyond it.


The entry is billed to the ticket's client; the client is not sent in the request. A ticket
with no client is rejected with 409, as it is in the app, which blocks logging time on such a
ticket. Assign a client to the ticket and the same request succeeds.


A client on credit hold cannot have time logged against it and is rejected with 409, as it is
in the app, which disables Add Time for such a client. Clear the credit hold and the same
request succeeds.


A closed ticket is rejected with 409 for the same reason: the app disables Add Time once a
ticket is closed. Solved, Merged and Cancelled tickets still accept time. Reopen the ticket
and the same request succeeds.

requestBody.description: Time entry to create, including the ticket to log it against.

get.summary: Gets a single time entry by id.
get.description:
The same shape as one item of `GET /v1/time-entries`, so a caller can follow up a page
with a single read, or re-read an entry after changing it, without a second mapping. The entry
is addressed by its id alone; the authenticated service provider is what scopes the lookup, so
an entry belonging to another service provider is reported as not found, and so is a deleted
one - the list does not show it either.

parameters.name: timeEntryId
parameters.description: Time entry to read.

patch.summary: Partially updates a time entry. Send only the fields you want to change.
patch.description:
Every field is optional and a field left out keeps its current value, so a body of `{}`
is accepted and returns the entry unchanged. Re-supplying a value the entry already holds is a
no-op: nothing is written, the entry's UpdatedOn does not move and no contract hours move.
The response is the updated entry, in the same shape `GET /v1/time-entries/{timeEntryId}` returns.


StartedOn, EndedOn and ActualHours are merged with the entry's current values before the same
any-two-of-three rule the create applies. Send two and the third is derived from those two;
send all three and they must agree. Send StartedOn or EndedOn alone and the other instant is
kept, so the duration changes with it; send ActualHours alone and StartedOn is kept and
EndedOn moves, so the duration is exactly what was sent.


Whenever the duration, work type, billing role, billable status or service line changes, the
entry is re-priced exactly as a new entry with the merged values would be: the work type's
minimum and increment rounding, the role's rate and the contract's terms are applied afresh,
and the hours the entry consumes from a BlockHours or LimitedHours contract are returned to
the old contract and drawn from the new. UserId, BillingRoleId, WorkTypeId, ServiceLineId
and BillableStatusId are validated the same way the create validates them.


The ticket an entry is logged against cannot be changed, and neither can its attachments: a
body carrying `TicketId` or `Attachments` is rejected with 400, as any unknown field
is. To move time to another ticket, delete the entry and log it against the other ticket.


Only a time entry that is still open can be changed. One that has been approved, completed or
invoiced is rejected with 409, as is one that is void. The ticket's own status does not matter:
time on a closed ticket that has not yet been billed can still be corrected here, exactly as the
Approve & Invoice flow corrects it, so there is nothing to reopen first. Reverse the approval
and the same request succeeds. Note that deleting such an entry is still refused while its
ticket is closed - correcting time and removing it are not the same act.

parameters.name: timeEntryId
parameters.description: Time entry to update.

delete.description:
The entry is addressed by its id alone; the authenticated service provider is what scopes the
lookup, so an entry belonging to another service provider is reported as not found.


Only a time entry that is still open can be deleted. One that has been approved, completed or
invoiced is rejected with 409, as is one that is void — deleting a settled entry would return it to the
open pipeline while an invoice still bills the same hours. Reversing an approved or invoiced
entry is a separate, explicit flow: delete the invoice item, then unapprove. An entry logged
against a ticket that is closed is rejected with 409 as well, whatever its own billing state —
reopen the ticket first.


For an entry that is still open, this behaves exactly as the app's delete does, which is a
two-step: an entry waiting for approval is returned to unclosed and stays where it is, and
deleting it again deactivates it and reverts its billing ledger. The response's
`outcome` says which happened — `Reopened` or `Deleted`. Deleting an entry that
is already deleted is accepted and reports `Deleted` without touching the ledger again.

parameters.name: timeEntryId
parameters.description: Time entry to delete.

get.summary: Lists billing contracts, each with the service lines it is made of.
get.description:
A contract is the agreement with a client; a service line is one set of labour terms and
products inside it. Most contracts have a single service line. A service line's id is the
same identifier a time entry's `ServiceLineId` carries, so a contract's service lines
are what a time entry can be billed against.


Service lines ride inside the contract rather than being fetched per contract, so a page of
contracts costs a fixed number of queries. Every filter is optional; the client filter is a
comma-separated list and a contract matches if its client is any of them. A well-formed value
that matches nothing - a client id that owns no contracts - is an empty page, not a 404.
Timestamps are UTC; `StartDate` and `EndDate` are stored as dates, so they are
always midnight.

`Status` is derived, because a contract has no stored status: `Archived` when the
contract has been archived, `Expired` when its end date is behind the service
provider's own today, and `Active` otherwise. Deleted contracts are not listed at all.
Archived and expired contracts are listed, so a caller that wants only live contracts should
keep the ones whose status is `Active`.

`RecurringAmount` and `RecurringCost` cover the products billed on the contract's
own recurring schedule, excluding one-off lines. Amount is before tax; cost is the unit cost
recorded against each product line multiplied by its quantity, so the difference between
them is the periodic margin. A contract's two figures are exactly the sum of its service
lines'.

`LaborTerms` says how a service line bills time - Unlimited Hours, Hourly, Block Hours,
No labor terms, or Limited Hours - and `LaborRates` says how an hour is priced for the
two that bill hourly, and is null for the rest.

parameters.name: Cursor
parameters.description: Opaque pagination cursor from a previous page; omit for the first page. Only valid against the same filters that produced it.

parameters.name: PageSize
parameters.description: Number of items per page. Clamped to 1-200 (default 50).

parameters.name: ClientIds
parameters.description: Comma-separated client ids; keeps only contracts billed to any of them.

get.summary: Everything about one contract, including each service line's actual products/labor.
get.description:
Adds the resolved `Client`, the invoice schedule (`DaysBeforeInvoiceCreation`,
`InvoiceDue`, `AutoApproveAndSend`), `Contacts`, and on each service line one
filled labor-terms-detail object (`UnlimitedHoursDetails`/`PerHourDetails`/
`LimitedHoursDetails`/`BlockHoursDetails`, matching `LaborTerms`) plus
`LineItems` — the actual products/labor billed on that line, empty when there's
nothing billed yet. A non-existent id, or one belonging to another service provider, is a
404.

parameters.name: contractId
parameters.description: Identifier of the contract.

delete.description:
Blocked with 409 if the contract has ever had an invoice generated from it — a contract
with real billing history can't be deleted by accident. Deleting a contract that's already
deleted is accepted as a no-op. A non-existent id, or one belonging to another service
provider, is a 404.

parameters.name: contractId
parameters.description: Identifier of the contract.

get.summary: Lists the service provider's invoices, filtered and sorted.
get.description:
Every filter is optional and combining two narrows to invoices that satisfy both. Each id
filter is a comma-separated list and an invoice matches if its id is any of them; a value
that is not an id is rejected with 400. A well-formed value that matches nothing is an empty
page, not a 404. Deleted invoices are never listed.

`SubTotal` is the line-item total before discount and tax; `Total` is
`SubTotal - TotalDiscount + TotalTax`. `AmountPaid` is computed live from recorded
payments, and `AmountDue` is `Total - AmountPaid`, floored at 0.

`InvoiceDate` and `DueDate` are calendar dates. `InvoiceDateSince`/`Before`
and `DueDateSince`/`Before` bound them the same way every other date filter on this
surface does: the lower bound includes the day it names and the upper bound excludes it.

`SortBy` is one of `createdOn` (default), `updatedOn`, `date` (InvoiceDate),
`dueDate` or `totalAmount`; `SortOrder` is `asc` or `desc` (default).

post.summary: Raises a manual invoice against a client, with line items.
post.description: Required: `ClientId`, and at least one line item with `ItemId` and `Quantity`. Optional:`StatusId` (defaults to Draft), `InvoiceDate` (defaults to today), `DueDate` (defaults to `InvoiceDate`), `Reference`, `RecipientEmails`. Per line: `UnitPrice`, `UnitCost`, `TaxId`, `CoaCode`, `Description`, `BillableStatusId` and `DiscountPercent` each fall back to the referenced item's own value when omitted. `StatusId` is `1` (Draft) or `5` (Approved). Approving on create also pushes the invoice to the connected accounting system. An Approved invoice whose total comes to exactly `0` is created as Paid instead - check `Status` on the response rather than assuming it matches what you sent. The response is just the created invoice's `Id` - the same shape Create Ticket and Create Time Entry return.

get.summary: Gets one invoice, with its attachments and line items.
get.description:
Same fields as `GET /v1/invoices`, plus `Description`, `Attachments` and
`LineItems`. An invoice that does not exist, or belongs to another service provider,
is a 404 - the two are never distinguished.


A bundle is one line: its quantity, price, cost, amount and tax are the bundle's, and
`SubItems` lists the items inside it. Every other line has `SubItems: []`.


Each attachment's `Url` is a temporary download link and expires - don't store it.

parameters.name: invoiceId
parameters.description: Invoice identifier.

delete.summary: Deletes or voids an invoice, depending on its current status.
delete.description:
Mirrors the app's own delete/void action on the invoice list - one endpoint, the outcome
depends on the invoice's current status:
<list type="table"><item><term>Draft</term><description>Deleted - the response's `StatusId` is 6
(Deleted), and the invoice is gone from `GET /v1/invoices` entirely.</description></item><item><term>Approved</term><description>Voided instead - the response's `StatusId` is
4 (Void), and the invoice stays visible on `GET /v1/invoices`.</description></item><item><term>Any other status</term><description>Refused with 409 - only a Draft or
Approved invoice can be removed this way.</description></item></list>

Deleting an invoice that's already deleted, or already void, is treated as success. An
invoice that doesn't exist, or belongs to another service provider, is a 404 - the two are
never distinguished.

parameters.name: invoiceId
parameters.description: Invoice identifier.

post.summary: Records a payment received outside Gorelo against an approved invoice.
post.description: Required: `InvoiceId`, `PaymentDate` and `Reference`. Optional:`Amount` - defaults to the invoice's whole amount due. It must be greater than 0 and no more than what the invoice still owes, so an invoice cannot be overpaid. `PaymentDate` is a calendar date and cannot be later than today in the service provider's time zone. The invoice must be Approved. A payment that leaves nothing owing marks the invoice Paid; otherwise its status is unchanged. The payment is added to the invoice's timeline and appears in `Payments` on `GET /v1/invoices/{invoiceId}`. Refused with 409 while the service provider has Xero or QuickBooks Online connected - record the payment there instead and it syncs to Gorelo. An invoice that doesn't exist, or belongs to another service provider, is a 404. The response is just the recorded payment's `Id`.

delete.summary: Deletes a payment that was recorded through the API.
delete.description:
Only a payment recorded through `POST /v1/payments` can be deleted; any other payment -
recorded in Gorelo or synced from an accounting system - is refused with 409. Also refused
with 409 while Xero or QuickBooks Online is connected.


If the payment had settled an invoice that now owes money again, the invoice goes back from
Paid to Approved. A payment that doesn't exist, has already been deleted, or belongs to
another service provider is a 404.

parameters.name: paymentId
parameters.description: Payment identifier.

get.summary: Lists the categories products are organised under, each with its subcategories.
get.description:
One level of nesting: a category holds subcategories, and a subcategory holds none.
`Subcategories` is always present and is an empty array for a category that has none.

`TaxId` is the tax rate assigned to the category, resolvable against
`GET /v1/taxes`, and null when none is assigned. A subcategory does not report one.


Only categories are listed at the top level, and deleted rows are not listed at all.
Category ids and subcategory ids are issued independently, so the same number can name one
of each - so a subcategory id is only meaningful alongside the category it is nested under.


The category surface is read-only: this list is the whole of it, and categories and
subcategories are created, changed and removed in the Gorelo app.

get.summary: Lists the service provider's item catalog: products and bundles.
get.description:
All filters are optional and combine with AND.


One resource for both kinds of item — `Type` says which. A bundle is a product made
of other products; an invoice line references either kind through one `ItemId`. Labor
items are internal to contract pricing, are not creatable in the app, and are never
returned here.

`Status` reflects whether the item is archived.

`CategoryId`, `SubcategoryId`, `ClientId` and `LocationId` are bare
ids — resolve a category/subcategory against `GET /v1/items/categories`.

parameters.name: Cursor
parameters.description: Opaque pagination cursor from a previous page; omit for the first page. Only valid against the same filters that produced it.

parameters.name: PageSize
parameters.description: Number of items per page. Rejected with a 400 outside 1-200 (default 50).

parameters.name: TypeIds
parameters.description: Comma-separated item type ids (1 Product, 2 Bundle).

post.summary: Creates a product or a bundle in the item catalog.
post.description: Required: `TypeId` (`1` Product or `2` Bundle) and `Name`. Product only:`Sku`, `PartNumber`, `Manufacturer`, `UnitCost`. Bundle only:`SubItems` (required for a bundle, at least one), `ShowSubItemsOnInvoice`, `ShowSubItemDescriptionsOnInvoice`. A bundle's `UnitCost` is calculated from its sub-items and can't be sent directly. Optional for either type:`Number`, `Description`, `CategoryId`, `SubcategoryId`, `ClientId`, `LocationId`, `Vendor`, `UnitPrice`, `TaxId`, `ExternalProductId`. Sending a Product-only field on a Bundle, or a Bundle-only field on a Product, is a 400. A `SubItems` entry can't itself be a bundle — bundles can't nest.

get.summary: A single catalog item — a product or a bundle.
get.description:
Adds `SubItems` over the list shape: the bundle's component products, each with the
quantity and the cost/price it carried when added. Present only for a bundle; null for a
product. A non-existent id, or one belonging to another service provider, is a 404.

parameters.name: itemId
parameters.description: Identifier of the item.

patch.summary: Partially updates an item. Send only the fields you want to change.
patch.description: All fields are optional — a field left out keeps its current value, so a body of `{}` is accepted and is a no-op. The response is just the item's `Id`, the same shape as `POST /v1/items` and `DELETE /v1/items/{itemId}` - fetch `GET /v1/items/{itemId}` separately to see the updated item. `TypeId` can never be changed — present in the body at all, including as `null`, is a 400. Which fields are accepted depends on the item's current type, the same Product/Bundle split as on create (see `POST /v1/items`). Clearing conventions, per field: `Name`, `Number`, `UnitPrice`, `UnitCost` and `StatusId` are not clearable — a supplied blank/invalid value is a 400, and `null` or omitting the field leaves it unchanged. `Description`, `Sku`, `PartNumber`, `Manufacturer`, `Vendor` and `ExternalProductId` are free text — an empty string clears the field, `null` or omitting it leaves it unchanged. `CategoryId`, `SubcategoryId`, `ClientId`, `LocationId` and `TaxId` clear via `0`; `null` or omitting the field leaves it unchanged. `SubItems` is bundle-only: an empty array clears the bundle down to no sub-items, `null` or omitting it leaves the current sub-items unchanged, and a non-empty array fully replaces them and recomputes `UnitCost`. Re-supplying a value the item already holds is a no-op.

parameters.name: itemId
parameters.description: Item to update.

delete.description:
Blocked with 409 if the item is a sub-item of any bundle, or is billed on any contract —
every blocker that applies is listed in the one response. Remove it from the
bundle(s)/contract(s) first, and the identical request then succeeds. An archived item
can be deleted.
Deleting a bundle does not delete its own sub-items. Being referenced on an existing
invoice does not block delete — an invoice line keeps its own frozen name, description and
money, independent of the item row.

parameters.name: itemId
parameters.description: Item to delete.

post.summary: Creates a contact under a client, or a temporary contact when no client is given.
post.description:
With a ClientId the contact belongs to that client. Without one it is created as a temporary
contact (IsTemporaryContact true) with no client and no location - the kind of contact an
email from an unknown requester creates - and it can be used as the contact or a cc contact
on a ticket that has no client. A LocationId needs a ClientId.
            
If another contact, active or temporary, already has the primary email address, nothing is
created and the response is a 409 whose message carries that contact's id: use it rather
than retrying. This endpoint never updates an existing contact.

get.summary: Lists the service provider's forms, most recently updated first.
get.description:
Ordered by when the form was last updated; no other sort is available. Active forms only, unless statusIds says otherwise. An archived form is
one deleted in the app - it is recoverable there, and readable here by id.
`ResponseCount` counts submitted responses; pending links and drafts are not counted.

get.description:
Cursor-paginated. Each response carries one answer per field that takes an answer, keyed
by the field's `Id` from the form detail; which of `TextValue`,
`NumberValue` and `OptionValues` is set follows the field's `Type`. Links
that were issued but never submitted are not responses and are not listed.

parameters.name: formId
parameters.description: Form whose responses to list.

parameters.name: Cursor
parameters.description: Opaque pagination cursor from a previous page; omit for the first page.

parameters.name: PageSize

post.summary: Issues a link through which the form can be submitted.
post.description:
The link opens the form in the Gorelo form web app without a login; one submission made
through it is filed against the form - and against the ticket or task named in the body,
if one is. Send at most one of `TicketId` and `TaskId`; both is a 400. Each must
be an active record of the authenticated service provider, or the response is a 400 naming
the field. An unused link expires at `ExpiresOn`, seven days after it is issued. An
archived form takes no submissions and is a 404, as is a form that does not exist or
belongs to another service provider.

parameters.name: formId
parameters.description: Form the link is for.

requestBody.description: The ticket or task the submission is for, optionally. An empty body is accepted as `{}`.

post.summary: Creates an API key for the authenticated service provider.
post.description:
Callable by any valid API key, whatever scopes it holds. The new key's scopes must be a
subset of the calling key's own, so a key can never create one more powerful than itself -
a key holding only `Tickets:read` can mint more `Tickets:read` keys and nothing
else. Asking for a scope the caller does not hold is rejected and names the scope.
            
Each requested scope is an explicit `"Module:verb"`; a bare module name is rejected.
The key value comes back on this response and on no other - only its hash is stored.

post.summary: Creates a project for the authenticated service provider.
post.description:
The project is created in the `NotStarted` status and numbered from the same sequence
the app uses, so its number and prefix match what the app would have given it. The same
creation timeline entry and the same project-created notification fire as when a project
is created in the app.
            
Groups are given as `GroupId` **or** `GroupIds` - exactly one of the two, and
sending both is a 400 rather than a silent choice between them.

get.summary: Gets a single project.
get.description:
Returns every field the project list returns, with the same values, plus the ones the list
leaves out: the project's `Description`, its `SharedWithContactIds` and its
`WatcherIds`.
            
A project's sections and tasks are their own sub-resources and are not embedded here - read
them from `GET /v1/projects/{projectId}/sections`.

parameters.name: projectId
parameters.description: Project identifier.

patch.summary: Updates a project. Send only the fields you want to change.
patch.description:
An omitted field is left alone; re-sending a value the project already holds is a no-op
rather than an error, and records no activity. Sending nothing at all is a 400.
            
Lists replace outright: send an empty array to clear one. `LeadAssigneeId: 0`
removes the lead, and `ClearTargetDate: true` removes the target date.
            
`ClosedOn` backdates the close of a project being migrated from another system, and
also becomes its `UpdatedOn`. It is only accepted for a project that is Closed -
already, or by this same request - and never for a future date or one before the project
was created. Omit it and closing a project stamps the time of the change; reopening a
Closed project clears it. Completed is reached automatically and carries no date.
            
Two field pairings are enforced because the data requires them: moving the project to a
different `ClientId` needs a `LocationId` in that client and **clears the
shared contacts**, and a technician cannot be both the lead and a watcher.

parameters.name: projectId
parameters.description: Project to update.

delete.summary: Deletes a project and every task in it.
delete.description:
A soft delete: the project and its tasks stop appearing and stop being targets for
automation, but the records and their history survive and can be recovered in the app.
The response says how many tasks went with it.

parameters.name: projectId
parameters.description: Project to delete.

get.summary: Lists the project tags configured for the service provider.
get.description:
Not paginated - a bounded set of configuration, the same class of list as the ticket
tags and types endpoints.
            
These are the ids a project's `TagIds` holds, and exactly the set
`POST`/`PATCH /v1/projects` will accept: a deleted tag is left out. Project
tags are their own set - they are not the ticket tags from `/v1/tickets/tags`, and
the two are keyed differently.

get.summary: Lists the project types configured for the service provider.
get.description:
Not paginated, for the reason given on the tags endpoint above. These are the ids a
project's `TypeId` takes, and exactly the set `POST`/`PATCH /v1/projects`
will accept: a deleted type is left out.

get.summary: Lists a project's sections.
get.description:
Not paginated. A section is a bounded lookup rather than a list of records - the largest
project in production has 23 sections - so the whole set is returned in one response, the
same way ticket statuses and types are.

parameters.name: projectId
parameters.description: Project identifier.

post.summary: Adds a section to a project.
post.description:
`Color` is optional - omit it and the section gets `#56A0F9`, the colour the
            app starts a new section from. Supplying it blank is still a 400: a section always has a
            colour.

parameters.name: projectId
parameters.description: Project to add the section to.

patch.summary: Updates a section's title or colour. Send only the fields you want to change.
patch.description:
Neither field is clearable - a section always has a title and a colour - so an omitted
field leaves the stored value alone and a supplied blank is rejected. Sending nothing at
all is a 400 rather than a no-op write.

parameters.name: projectId
parameters.description: Project the section belongs to.

parameters.name: sectionId
parameters.description: Section to update.

delete.summary: Deletes a section and every task in it.
delete.description:
The tasks go with the section. Leaving them behind would strand them: on no board, still
counted in the project's totals, and still a target for automation. The response says how
many were deactivated.

parameters.name: projectId
parameters.description: Project the section belongs to.

parameters.name: sectionId
parameters.description: Section to delete.

get.description:
Ordered by the board's own ordering by default, so the response matches what the app
shows. The locked contract's `assignedToMe` is not offered: the gateway strips
every technician identifier, so "me" would resolve to nobody and the filter would match
nothing for every key. Use assigneeIds instead.

parameters.name: projectId
parameters.description: Project whose tasks to list.

parameters.name: Cursor
parameters.description: Opaque pagination cursor from a previous page; omit for the first page.

parameters.name: PageSize
parameters.description: Number of items per page, 1-200 (default 50). Out of range is rejected, not clamped.

parameters.name: SortBy
parameters.description: Sort field: `boardOrder` (default), `createdOn` or `updatedOn`.

parameters.name: SortOrder
parameters.description: Sort direction: `asc` (default) or `desc`.

parameters.name: SectionIds
parameters.description: Comma-separated section ids (Guids).

parameters.name: StatusIds
parameters.description: Comma-separated status ids: NotStarted=1, WorkingOnIt=2, OnHold=3, Done=4.

parameters.name: AssigneeIds
parameters.description: Comma-separated technician ids; matches a task's lead or assisting assignees.

parameters.name: LeadAssigneeIds

post.summary: Creates a task on a project's board.
post.description:
The task is numbered from the project's own sequence, so its display number matches what
the app would have given it - `PRO-462-7`. Creating a task moves a project that had
not started into progress, exactly as it does in the app, and fires the same automation
triggers.
            
`PriorityId` is the same scale a ticket uses: None=0, Urgent=1, High=2, Normal=3,
Low=4. Omit it for Normal.

parameters.name: projectId
parameters.description: Project to create the task in.

post.summary: Posts a comment on a project.
post.description:
Comments default to `ConversationTypeId: 2` (Private). A project has no side
conversations or approvals, so `3` and `4` are rejected.
            
Attach files by uploading them first and sending back the
name and url you were given; any access token on a url is stripped before storage and a
fresh one is issued whenever the comment is read, so never store the url you get back.

parameters.name: projectId
parameters.description: Project to comment on.

get.summary: Returns a project's comments, newest first.
get.description:
Cursor-paginated. Attachment and inline-image links carry a time-limited access token
that expires, so fetch the comment again rather than storing a url.
            
Rows carry `BodyTruncated` so this list has the same shape as the task comment list,
but it is always false here: a project comment's body is always inline, so the full body
is in the row and there is nothing further to fetch.

parameters.name: projectId
parameters.description: Project whose comments to return.

parameters.name: Cursor
parameters.description: Cursor from a previous page.

parameters.name: PageSize
parameters.description: Comments per page, 1-200. Defaults to 50.

parameters.name: SortOrder
parameters.description: `desc` (default, newest first) or `asc`.

get.summary: Returns one comment on a project.

parameters.name: projectId
parameters.description: Project the comment belongs to.

parameters.name: commentId
parameters.description: Comment to return.

delete.summary: Deletes one comment on a project.
delete.description:
A soft delete: the comment stops appearing but the record survives. Deleting a comment
that is already deleted succeeds and writes nothing.
            
Only a private comment can be deleted - the product has no delete for a public comment
anywhere, including the app - so a public one is refused with `ResourceNotDeletable`.

parameters.name: projectId
parameters.description: Project the comment belongs to.

parameters.name: commentId
parameters.description: Comment to delete.

get.summary: Returns one task in full.
get.description:
Everything the project's task list returns, plus the fields that live only on the task
itself: linked assets, blocking relationships in both directions, the reason behind its
status, and time recorded against it.
            
A task in a project you cannot see returns 404, the same as one that does not exist.

parameters.name: projectId
parameters.description: Project the task belongs to.

parameters.name: taskId
parameters.description: Task to return.

patch.summary: Updates a task. Send only the fields you want to change.
patch.description:
An omitted field is left alone; re-sending a value the task already holds is a no-op
rather than an error, and records no activity. Sending nothing at all is a 400.
            
Lists replace outright: send an empty array to clear one. `LeadAssigneeId: 0`
removes the lead, and `ClearDueDate: true` removes the due date - a date field is
never cleared by omission.
            
Changing the status fires the same automation the app fires.

parameters.name: projectId
parameters.description: Project the task belongs to.

parameters.name: taskId
parameters.description: Task to update.

delete.description:
A soft delete: the task stops appearing anywhere and stops being a target for
automation, but its history survives and it can be recovered in the app.
            
Blocking relationships are cleared in both directions, so no other task is left pointing
at it, and any automation timer waiting on it is dropped.

parameters.name: projectId
parameters.description: Project the task belongs to.

parameters.name: taskId
parameters.description: Task to delete.

post.summary: Posts a comment on a task.
post.description:
Comments default to `ConversationTypeId: 2` (Private). Any other kind is
outward-facing, so posting one puts the task in a waiting-on-the-contact state and fires
the same automation the app does.
            
Side Conversation (3) and Approval (4) need the `ConversationId` of a conversation
that already exists on this task - list them with the conversations endpoint.
            
Attach files by uploading them first and sending back the name and url you were given.
Any access token on a url is stripped before storage and a fresh one is issued whenever
the comment is read, so never store the url you get back.

parameters.name: projectId
parameters.description: Project the task belongs to.

parameters.name: taskId
parameters.description: Task to comment on.

get.summary: Returns a task's comments, newest first.
get.description:
Cursor-paginated. Filter from broadest to narrowest: send nothing for every comment;
conversationType to select kinds; or a single
conversationType together with conversationId for
one specific conversation.
            
Attachment and inline-image links carry a time-limited access token that expires, so
fetch the comment again rather than storing a url.
            
A comment that arrived by email stores its body outside the document, and this list does
not fetch it: such a row carries `BodyTruncated: true` with an empty
`BodyHtml`/`BodyText`. Read the single comment to get the full body.

parameters.name: projectId
parameters.description: Project the task belongs to.

parameters.name: taskId
parameters.description: Task whose comments to return.

parameters.name: Cursor
parameters.description: Cursor from a previous page.

parameters.name: PageSize
parameters.description: Comments per page, 1-200. Defaults to 50.

parameters.name: SortBy
parameters.description: Sort field: `createdOn`.

parameters.name: SortOrder
parameters.description: `desc` (default, newest first) or `asc`.

parameters.name: ConversationType
parameters.description: Kinds to include: `1` Public, `2` Private, `3` Side Conversation, `4` Approval. Comma-separated on its own; a single value when paired with conversationId.

parameters.name: ConversationId
parameters.description: Identifier of the single conversation to read, from the conversations endpoint. Requires a single conversationType.

post.summary: Starts a side conversation on a task.
post.description:
A thread with somebody outside the task's own contacts - a vendor, say. The conversation
is created empty; its messages are posted afterwards.

parameters.name: projectId
parameters.description: Project the task belongs to.

parameters.name: taskId
parameters.description: Task to start the conversation on.

post.summary: Asks contacts to approve something on a task.
post.description:
Each contact must be an active contact of the task's client **and** carry a contact tag
marked as an approver - the same constraint the app's picker applies. A contact that is
not eligible is rejected before anything is written.
            
Creating an approval puts the task in a waiting-on-the-contact state.

parameters.name: projectId
parameters.description: Project the task belongs to.

parameters.name: taskId
parameters.description: Task the approval is for.

requestBody.description: What is being approved, and by whom.

get.summary: Returns one comment on a task.
get.description:
Always returns the whole body, so there is no `BodyTruncated` field: a body stored
outside the document - an emailed-in comment - is read back here. If that stored body
cannot be reached, `BodyHtml` is null rather than empty, to distinguish a body that
is unavailable from a comment that has none.

parameters.name: projectId
parameters.description: Project the task belongs to.

parameters.name: taskId
parameters.description: Task the comment belongs to.

parameters.name: commentId
parameters.description: Comment to return.

delete.summary: Deletes one comment on a task.
delete.description:
A soft delete, and idempotent: deleting a comment that is already deleted succeeds and
writes nothing. Only a private comment can be deleted - anything outward-facing (public,
a side conversation, an approval) has left the tenant and is refused with
`ResourceNotDeletable`.

parameters.name: projectId
parameters.description: Project the task belongs to.

parameters.name: taskId
parameters.description: Task the comment belongs to.

parameters.name: commentId
parameters.description: Comment to delete.

get.summary: Lists the conversations on a task.
get.description:
Public and Private are the task's main thread and come back with a null `Id`; Side
Conversation and Approval carry a real `Id` that can be passed to the comments
endpoint as `conversationId`. Type-specific details live on each type's own detail
endpoint, so every row has the same lean shape.
            
Not paginated, matching the ticket equivalent: the set is one task's own conversations.

parameters.name: projectId
parameters.description: Project the task belongs to.

the Recycle Bin, never removed. Its delayed actions are cleared, scheduled automation is
cancelled and it leaves the search index, exactly as when it is deleted in the app.

returned to the contract. If any of those time entries has already been approved, completed, voided
or invoiced the whole request is refused with 409 and nothing is deleted; the message lists

of that, so a retried request is safe.

Backdate the ticket's creation timestamp — for importing tickets from another system.
Must not be in the future. Omit to use the current time. Required when ClosedOn or
UpdatedOn is supplied. A caller migrating a ticket sends CreatedOn, ClosedOn and UpdatedOn
together, so the ticket keeps the dates it had in the other system.

ClosedOn.description:
The date the ticket was closed, for importing already-closed tickets from another system.
Requires CreatedOn to be supplied. Only valid when the ticket is created in a closed status.
Must not be in the future or earlier than CreatedOn. Omit to have a ticket created in a

live work. Requires CreatedOn to be supplied. Must not be in the future or earlier than

ClientId.description: Identifier of the client the ticket belongs to.

LocationId.description: Identifier of the client location the ticket belongs to. Requires ClientId.

ContactId.description:
Identifier of the primary contact for the ticket. With a ClientId it must be a contact of
that client; without one it must be a temporary contact (IsTemporaryContact true).

CcContactIds.description:
Identifiers of additional (CC) contacts. At most 100. Same rule as ContactId: contacts of
the ticket's client, or temporary contacts when the ticket has no client.

StatusId.description: Initial status identifier. Required; must be an existing status for the service provider.

GroupId.description: Identifier of the technician group the ticket is assigned to. Required.

WatcherIds.description: Identifiers of technicians watching the ticket.

TagIds.description: Identifiers of tags to apply to the ticket.

AgentAssetIds.description: Identifiers of agent (managed device) assets to link to the ticket.

CustomAssetIds.description: Identifiers of custom assets to link to the ticket.

UptimeIds.description: Identifiers of uptime monitors to link to the ticket.

SendTicketCreatedEmail.description: When true, sends a "ticket created" email to the contact. Defaults to false.

IsUnread.description: Whether the ticket is created in an unread state. Defaults to true.

CreateTicketCommand.description:
Request body for creating a ticket. The owning service provider is resolved from the
request context, not from the body.

Id.description: Identifier of the newly created ticket.

TicketId.description:
Ticket to log the time against. Send **either** this or `TaskId`, not both and
not neither. Validated against the service provider - an unknown ticket is a 404. The entry
is billed to the ticket's client; a ticket with no client is rejected with 409.

TaskId.description:
Task to log the time against, instead of a ticket. Validated the same way - an unknown task
is a 404. The entry is billed to the client of the task's **project**, which is
authoritative; the task's own copy of the client can lag behind.
            
A task carries no billing defaults of its own, so the billing role, work type and billable
status fall to the technician's defaults and then the service provider's - the same chain a
ticket uses once its own values are absent.

StartedOn.description:
When the work started, as a single UTC instant.
            
Supply any two of StartedOn, EndedOn and ActualHours and the third is derived. Supplying all
three is accepted only when ActualHours agrees with the span between the two instants, to the
same four decimal places GET reports it at; a disagreement is rejected rather than resolved
by discarding one of the three.

EndedOn.description:
When the work finished, as a single UTC instant. Must be later than `StartedOn`.
See `StartedOn` for which combinations of the three time fields are accepted.

ActualHours.description:
Duration worked, in decimal hours. Must be greater than 0.
            
This is the raw logged duration and is never pre-rounded: the work type's minimum and
increment rounding is applied on top of it, and GET reports the rounded figure separately as
AdjustedHours. See `StartedOn` for which combinations of the three time fields
are accepted.

BillableStatusId.description:
Billable status for this entry: 1 = Billable, 2 = No charge, 3 = Non-billable; any other
value is rejected. Optional — omit it and the ticket's own billable status is used, else the
work type's, else Billable.

UserId.description:
User whose time this is. Validated against the service provider. Named UserId rather than
TechnicianId because Gorelo uses "user", not "technician", in its own vocabulary.

BillingRoleId.description:
Billing role to charge at. Optional — omit it and the ticket's own billing role is used, else
the user's, else the service provider's first. Get valid ids from
GET /v1/billing-roles.

WorkTypeId.description:
Work type to apply. Determines the rate multiplier and the minimum/increment rounding applied
to the logged duration. Optional — omit it and the ticket's own work type is used, else the
user's, else the service provider's first. Get valid ids from
GET /v1/work-types.

ServiceLineId.description:
Service line to bill this time against.
            
Optional. Omit it and the ticket's own service line is used, else the first one whose
configured billing roles and work types both cover the resolved role and type, else no
contract. Send it as null to decline a contract outright, which suppresses the automatic
contract assignment that would otherwise happen when the time is approved.
            
When supplied, the service line must belong to the ticket's client, and its contract must
be active today and cover labour.

Distance.description: Distance travelled for this work, when the service provider bills mileage.

Attachments.description: Files to attach to this entry. The serialised list must be 5000 characters or fewer.

Id.description: Identifier of the created time entry.

TypeId.description: What the check does: 1 ICMP, 2 HTTP, 3 TCP. Required.

AdoptClientAssets.description:
Move unassigned devices whose public IP matches this check's address to the check's
client. Only acted on for ICMP checks that carry both a client and a location; stored
either way.

ClientId.description:
Identifier of the client the check belongs to. When supplied, `LocationId`
is required with it.

LocationId.description: Identifier of the client location the check belongs to.

Description.description: What the check watches, free text. Max 250 characters.

Frequency.description: How often the check runs, in minutes. Required.

NumberOfRetriesAfterFailure.description: How many times a failure is rechecked before the check counts as down. Defaults to 2.

RegionId.description: Which monitoring region runs the check: 1 Seattle, 2 Sydney, 3 UK, 4 Frankfurt. Required.

IspConnectionLink.description: Link to the ISP or provider status page for this endpoint. Max 500 characters.

TagIds.description: Identifiers of tags to apply to the check.

CreateUptimeCheckCommand.description:
Request body for creating an uptime check. The owning service provider is resolved from the
request context, not from the body.

CreateUptimeCheckResult.description: The identifier of the created uptime check.

ClientId.description: Identifier of the client the asset belongs to.

LocationId.description: Identifier of the client location the asset belongs to.

UpdatedOn.description: Last-updated timestamp (UTC).

CustomAssetResponse.description: A custom (non-agent) asset. Timestamps are UTC.

StatusId.description:
The invoice's status after the call: 6 (Deleted) when a Draft invoice was deleted, or 4
(Void) when an Approved invoice was voided. Deleted (6) appears only here - a deleted
invoice is never returned by `GET /v1/invoices`, so the list's status set stays 1-5.

DeleteInvoiceResult.description: The outcome of deleting an invoice.

DeletePaymentResult.description: The outcome of deleting a payment.

DeleteProjectCommentResult.description: The identifier of the deleted comment.

DeletedTaskCount.description: Tasks deactivated as part of the delete.

DeleteProjectResult.description: The identifier of the deleted project, and how many tasks went with it.

DeletedTaskCount.description: Tasks deactivated as part of the delete.

DeleteSectionResult.description: The identifier of the deleted section, and how many tasks went with it.

DeleteTaskCommentResult.description: The identifier of the deleted comment.

DeleteTaskResult.description: The identifier of the deleted task.

Outcome.description:
What the delete actually did. A time entry that has been closed for billing is first pulled
back out of the billing pipeline — the same two-step the app has — so a single DELETE does not
always remove the entry. Without this field both outcomes would look like an identical 200
while the entry was still listed.

`Deleted` — the entry is now inactive and its billing ledger entries reverted.
`Reopened` — the entry was closed for billing and has been returned to unclosed;
delete it again to remove it.

ShowSubItemDescriptionsOnInvoice.description: Bundle-only. Rejected (400) if sent while the item is a product.

UpdateItemCommand.description:
Partial update of an item. Every field is optional and only the fields present in the body are
applied. Per-field clearing conventions:
<list type="bullet"><item>Name, Number, UnitPrice, UnitCost, StatusId — not clearable: a supplied blank/invalid
value is a 400, omit or send null to leave unchanged.</item><item>Description, Sku, PartNumber, Manufacturer, Vendor, ExternalProductId — free text: an
empty string clears it, null/omitted leaves it unchanged.</item><item>CategoryId, SubcategoryId, ClientId, LocationId, TaxId — id fields: 0 clears it,
null/omitted leaves it unchanged.</item><item>SubItems — an empty array clears the bundle's sub-items, null/omitted leaves them
unchanged, a non-empty array fully replaces them.</item></list>
TypeId is not accepted at all - present in the body (any value, including null) is a 400.

Description.description: New description. Send an empty string to remove it.

ClientId.description:
Move the project to a different client. **Clears the shared contacts**, because a contact
belongs to the client it came from - the app does the same.
Send `LocationId` with it: a location belongs to a client.

LocationId.description: New client location.

SharedWithContactIds.description: Replaces the contacts the project is shared with. Empty array clears them.

TagIds.description: Replaces the tags. Empty array clears them.

LeadAssigneeId.description: New lead assignee. Send 0 to remove the lead.

WatcherIds.description: Replaces the watchers. Empty array clears them.

GroupIds.description: Replaces the technician groups the project belongs to.

TargetDate.description: New target date (UTC). To remove it, send `ClearTargetDate`.

ClearTargetDate.description: Set true to remove the due date.

StatusId.description:
New status: Not Started=1, In Progress=2, On Hold=3, Completed=4, Closed=5. Completed is
normally reached automatically once every task is Done; Closed is the manual end state
and stamps `ClosedOn`. Moving a Closed project to any other status clears it.

StatusReason.description: Free-text reason recorded with the status. Only read when `StatusId` is sent.

ClosedOn.description:
The date the project was closed (UTC), for recording the real close date of a project
migrated from another system. The project must already be Closed, or be moved into that
status by this same request. Must not be in the future or earlier than the project's
`CreatedOn`. A supplied date also becomes the project's `UpdatedOn`. Omit it to
leave the date untouched - closing a project normally stamps it with the time of the change.

UpdatedByName.description:
Display name to record as the actor. An API key is not a person, so when it is
omitted or blank the actor is recorded as `API`.

UpdateProjectCommand.description:
Request body for updating a project. Every field is optional - send only what you want to
change. An omitted field leaves the stored value alone; sending nothing at all is a 400.

UpdateProjectResult.description: The identifier of the updated project.

Title.description: New section title. Omit to leave unchanged.

Color.description: New colour, as the app stores it. Omit to leave unchanged.

UpdatedByName.description: Display name to record as the author of this change. Omitted or blank, it is recorded as `API`.

UpdateSectionCommand.description:
Request body for updating a section. Both fields are optional; send only what you want to
change.
            
Neither field is clearable: a section always has a title and a colour, so an omitted field
leaves the stored value alone and a supplied blank is rejected.

UpdateSectionResult.description: The identifier of the updated section.

SectionId.description: Section to move the task to. Must be an active section of the same project.

StatusId.description: New status: NotStarted=1, WorkingOnIt=2, OnHold=3, Done=4.

StatusReason.description: Free-text reason recorded with the status. Only read when `StatusId` is sent.

PriorityId.description: New priority: None=0, Urgent=1, High=2, Normal=3, Low=4 - the ticket scale.

DueDate.description: New due date (UTC). Send null to leave it alone; to clear it, send `ClearDueDate`.

ClearDueDate.description: Set true to remove the due date. A task's due date is otherwise never cleared by omission.

LeadAssigneeId.description: New lead assignee. Send 0 to remove the lead.

AssistingAssigneeIds.description: Replaces the assisting assignees outright. Send an empty array to remove them all.

WatcherIds.description: Replaces the watchers outright. Send an empty array to remove them all.

BlockedByTaskIds.description: Replaces the tasks that must finish before this one can.

BlockingTaskIds.description: Replaces the tasks this one is blocking.

Banner.description: New banner text. Send an empty string to remove it.

UpdatedByName.description:
Display name to record as the actor. An API key is not a person, so when it is
omitted or blank the actor is recorded as `API`.

UpdateTaskCommand.description:
Request body for updating a task. Every field is optional - send only what you want to
change. An omitted field leaves the stored value alone; sending nothing at all is a 400
rather than a no-op write.

UpdateTaskResult.description: The identifier of the updated task.

UpdatedByName.description: Display name recorded as the author of this update. Source is always stamped as Public API. Omitted or blank, it is recorded as `API`.

ClosedOn.description:
The date the ticket was closed, for correcting the close date of a ticket migrated from
another system. The ticket must already be in a closed status, or be moved into one by this
same request. Must not be in the future or earlier than the ticket's CreatedOn. Omit to leave
an already-closed ticket's close date untouched. Sending null is the same as omitting it -
the close date is not clearable here, since a closed ticket always has one.

UpdatedOn.description:
Timestamp to record as the ticket's last activity instead of the current time, for a
caller replaying historical changes. Must not be in the future or earlier than the
ticket's CreatedOn. Applies to whichever fields this request changes; it is not an
update on its own. Defaults to the ClosedOn supplied by the same request, otherwise to the
current time. A caller migrating a ticket sends CreatedOn on create, and ClosedOn and
UpdatedOn together here, so the ticket keeps the dates it had in the other system. Sending
null is the same as omitting it.

ClientId.description: Client the ticket belongs to. Changing it clears the ticket's contact, assets, uptime checks and billing override.

LocationId.description: Client location the ticket belongs to. Requires the ticket to have a client.

ContactId.description:
Primary contact on the ticket. Must be a contact of the ticket's client (the ClientId sent,
otherwise the one the ticket has); a ticket with no client takes a temporary contact
(IsTemporaryContact true).

CcContactIds.description:
Cc contacts on the ticket. At most 100. Same rule as ContactId: contacts of the ticket's
client, or temporary contacts when the ticket has no client.

GroupIds.description: Technician groups subscribed to the ticket.

AgentAssetIds.description: Agent (managed device) asset ids to link. Replaces the current set; omit to leave unchanged.

CustomAssetIds.description: Custom asset ids to link. Replaces the current set; omit to leave unchanged.

UptimeIds.description: Uptime check ids to link. Replaces the current set; omit to leave unchanged.

UpdateTicketCommand.description:
Unified partial update for a ticket. Every field is optional; only the fields present in the
request body are applied. Each change has the same effects (notifications, timeline entries)
as making it in the app.

StartedOn.description:
When the work started, as a single UTC instant.
            
The three time fields are merged with the entry's current values before the same
any-two-of-three rule the create applies. Send two of them and the third is derived from
those two alone; send all three and they must agree. Send StartedOn or EndedOn alone and the
other instant is kept, so the duration changes with it. Send ActualHours alone and StartedOn
is kept and EndedOn moves, so the duration is exactly what was sent. Sending null is the same
as omitting it - neither instant is clearable, since an entry always has an interval.

EndedOn.description:
When the work finished, as a single UTC instant. Must be later than the StartedOn in force
after the merge. See `StartedOn` for how the three time fields combine. Sending null is
the same as omitting it.

ActualHours.description:
Duration worked, in decimal hours. Must be greater than 0. The work type's minimum and
increment rounding is applied on top of it, as on create. See `StartedOn` for how the
three time fields combine.

BillableStatusId.description:
Billable status for this entry: 1 = Billable, 2 = No charge, 3 = Non-billable; any other
value is rejected.

UserId.description:
User whose time this is. Validated against the service provider. Changing it re-stamps the
entry's cost rate from the new user's own rate, as the app does.

BillingRoleId.description:
Billing role to charge at. Validated against the service provider's active roles. Get valid
ids from GET /v1/billing-roles.

WorkTypeId.description:
Work type to apply. Determines the rate multiplier and the minimum/increment rounding applied
to the logged duration. Validated against the service provider's active work types. Get
valid ids from GET /v1/work-types.

ServiceLineId.description:
Service line to bill this time against.
            
Omit it and the entry keeps the service line it has. Send it as null to take the entry off
its contract outright, which also suppresses the automatic contract assignment that would
otherwise happen when the time is approved. When supplied, the service line must belong to
the entry's client, and its contract must be active today and cover labour. Moving an entry
between contracts returns the hours it consumed to the old one and draws them from the new.

Comment.description: Free-text note describing the work. Send an empty string to clear it.

Distance.description: Distance travelled for this work, when the service provider bills mileage.

UpdateTimeEntryCommand.description:
Partial update of a time entry. Every field is optional and only the fields present in the body
are applied; a field left out keeps its current value. The ticket an entry is logged against and
its attachments cannot be changed here, so neither is a member: a body carrying either is
rejected as malformed, the same way every other endpoint treats a field it does not know.

TypeId.description:
What the check does: 1 ICMP, 2 HTTP, 3 TCP. Changing this requires sending a
`Target` valid for the new type, because the two are stored together.

AdoptClientAssets.description: Move matching unassigned devices to the check's client. See the create request.

ClientId.description:
Identifier of the client the check belongs to. Sending this without
`LocationId` is rejected, because a location belongs to a client and moving
one without the other would file the check at the old client's site.

LocationId.description: Identifier of the client location the check belongs to.

Description.description: What the check watches, free text. Max 250 characters.

Frequency.description: How often the check runs, in minutes.

NumberOfRetriesAfterFailure.description: How many times a failure is rechecked before the check counts as down.

RegionId.description:
Which monitoring region runs the check. Changing it cancels the check's schedule in the
old region and schedules it in the new one.

IspConnectionLink.description: Link to the ISP or provider status page for this endpoint.

TagIds.description:
Replaces the check's tags outright. An empty array clears them; omitting the field leaves
them alone.

UpdateUptimeCheckCommand.description:
Request body for updating an uptime check. Every field is optional - send only what should
change. An omitted field keeps the value the check already holds.

UpdateUptimeCheckResult.description: The identifier of the updated uptime check.

Enabled.description:
Whether the check is currently in maintenance mode. When false, the remaining fields
are null.

DurationInMinutes.description: How long the window lasts, in minutes. Zero means the window does not expire on its own.

Reason.description: Why the check was put into maintenance. Max 500 characters.

UptimeMaintenanceMode.description:
A check's maintenance window - the period its failures are suppressed for.


Field names match the ones the update request takes.

Description.description: Free-text description of what the check watches. Max 250 characters.

AdoptClientAssets.description:
Whether unassigned devices whose public IP matches this check's address are moved to the
check's client. Not part of `Target`. Only acted on for ICMP checks that
carry both a client and a location.

ClientId.description: Identifier of the client the check belongs to.

LocationId.description: Identifier of the client location the check belongs to.

Frequency.description: How often the check runs, in minutes.

NumberOfRetriesAfterFailure.description: How many times a failure is rechecked before the check is treated as down.

RegionId.description: Which monitoring region runs the check: 1 Seattle, 2 Sydney, 3 UK, 4 Frankfurt.

IspConnectionLink.description: Link to the ISP or provider status page for this endpoint. Max 500 characters.

TagIds.description: Identifiers of the tags applied to the check.

UpdatedOn.description: Last-updated timestamp (UTC).

UptimeResponse.description: An uptime check. Timestamps are UTC.

Ip.description:
Host to ping, for ICMP and TCP checks. ICMP accepts a hostname as well as an address;
TCP requires a parseable address.

Port.description: Port to connect to, for TCP checks.

Url.description: Address to request, for HTTP checks.

UptimeTarget.description:
What an uptime check points at. Which fields are populated depends on the check type:
ICMP uses `Ip`, TCP uses `Ip` and `Port`, HTTP uses
`Url`. The others are null.

UpdatedOn.description: Last-updated timestamp (UTC).

TimeZone.description: IANA time zone identifier for the user.

UserModel.description: A user (technician) in the service provider organization. Timestamps are UTC.

Id.description: Identifier of the work type. Send this as WorkTypeId when logging time.

Name.description: Display name of the work type.

HourlyMultiplier.description: Multiplier applied to the billing role's hourly rate for this work type.

IsDefaultOutsideBusinessHours.description: Whether this is the work type applied by default to off-hours time.

CoaCode.description: Chart-of-accounts code this work type posts to, when one is configured.

MinimumTimeInMinutes.description: Shortest billable duration, in minutes. An entry shorter than this is rounded up to it.

IncrementTimeInMinutes.description:
Billing increment, in minutes. An entry longer than the minimum is rounded up to the next
whole increment. Zero means no rounding is applied.

WorkTypeModel.description: A work type configured for the service provider.

tags.name: Attachments
tags.description:
Uploading a file, for anything that can carry one. One endpoint rather than one per record
type, because the upload itself is identical - only the record it is checked against differs.
